147	
148	- `.` matches a whole multi-byte character (é = 2 bytes → one `X`).
149	- `\w`, `\d`, `\b` are Unicode-aware.
150	
151	```
152	printf 'héllo'       | /workspace/executable '.' 'X'    ->  X X X X X          (5 replacements, é = one match)
153	printf 'héllo wörld' | /workspace/executable '\w+' 'X'  ->  X   X              (é, ö are word chars)
154	printf 'é'           | /workspace/executable '\w' 'X'   ->  X
155	printf '٣'           | /workspace/executable '\d' 'X'   ->  X                  (Arabic-Indic digit matches \d)
156	printf 'aé b'        | /workspace/executable '\b' '|'   ->  | a 303 251 |   | b |   (\b treats é as word char)
157	printf 'éÉ'          | /workspace/executable -f i 'é' 'X' ->  X X              (Unicode case folding under -f i)
158	```
159	
160	## 10. Case and word flags (brief)
161	
162	```
163	printf 'aA'     | /workspace/executable 'a' 'X'        ->  X A      (case-sensitive by default)
164	printf 'aA'     | /workspace/executable -f i 'a' 'X'   ->  X X
165	printf 'cat at' | /workspace/executable -f w 'at' 'X'  ->  c a t   X   (-f w wraps pattern in \b...\b)
166	```
167	
168	## 11. Unsupported regex features (exit 1, error on stderr, stdout empty)
169	
170	```
171	printf 'ab' | /workspace/executable 'a(?=b)' 'X'
172	  exit=1, stderr:
173	  error: invalid regex regex parse error:\n    a(?=b)\n       ^^^\nerror: look-around, including look-ahead and look-behind, is not supported\n
174	
175	printf 'aa' | /workspace/executable '(a)\1' 'X'
176	  exit=1, stderr:
177	  error: invalid regex regex parse error:\n    (a)\1\n        ^^\nerror: backreferences are not supported\n
178	```
179	
180	(Error text shown with `\n` denoting literal newlines; the caret line aligns under the offending token. Exact byte stream: `error: invalid regex regex parse error:\n    a(?=b)\n       ^^^\nerror: look-around, including look-ahead and look-behind, is not supported\n`.)
181	
182	## 12. Misc
183	
184	- No match found → exit 0, input echoed unchanged (`printf 'abc' | sd 'z' 'X'` → `abc`, exit 0).
185	- Empty stdin with non-matching pattern → empty stdout, exit 0.
186	- `$$` in replacement → literal `$` (`printf 'foo' | sd 'foo' '$$bar'` → `$bar`).
187	- `-F` fixed-strings: find is literal, and a literal newline in the find arg works (`-F 'a\nb'` with real newline matched `a\nb`).
188	
189	## 13. Performance sanity
190	
191	- 11.25 MB file (`abcdefgh\n` × 1.25M), pattern `a.c` → in-place rewrite in **~0.135 s**, 8.75 MB output correct.
192	- ~112 MB piped through stdin, pattern `a.c` → **~0.14 s**. Streaming/fast, linear in input size.
193	- Pathological pattern `(a+)+$` on `'a'×30 + 'b'` → **0.006 s**, exit 0. No catastrophic backtracking (finite-automata engine, linear-time guarantee).
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Summary of the model to reimplement
198	
199	The behavior is exactly the Rust `regex` crate (bytes API) with: multi_line = ON by default (`-f e` turns it off, `-f m` on), dot_matches_new_line = OFF by default (`-f s` on), case_insensitive OFF (`-f i` on, `-f c` forces sensitive), `-f w` wraps in `\b(?:...)\b`-style word boundaries. Replacement = `replacen`-style global replace with the standard "skip empty match that coincides with previous match end, else advance one char" iteration. Input = whole buffer (stdin slurped or file memory-mapped/read whole), arbitrary bytes allowed, invalid UTF-8 passes through untouched.

1	# sd 1.0.0 — File-Mode Behavior (Black-Box Probing Report)
2	
3	Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`sd 1.0.0`). All probes run in `/workspace/probe/t*/`.
4	All commands were run under `bash` on Linux as `root` unless noted (some as user
5	`nobody` via `runuser -u nobody --`). Byte dumps are `od -c` output of captured
6	stdout/stderr or of the file itself. Exit codes captured with `echo $?`.
7	
8	Conventions below: `stdout: empty` / `stderr: empty` mean zero bytes.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Basic in-place modification
13	
14	Command:
15	```sh
16	printf 'hello world\nfoo world\n' > basic.txt
17	/workspace/executable 'world' 'WORLD' basic.txt > out.bin 2> err.bin
18	```
19	- exit code: `0`
20	- stdout: empty (zero bytes). stderr: empty (zero bytes).
21	- resulting file bytes (od -c):
22	  ```
23	  h e l l o   W O R L D \n f o o   W O R L D \n
24	  ```
25	- **Inode changes** (85077922 → 85077974): the file is not written in place; it is
26	  replaced by a new file (temp-file + rename, see §7).
27	- File mode **never** echoes the result to stdout (except with `-p`, see §14).
28	
29	## 2. Trailing newline handling / empty file
30	
31	- File with trailing newline: `printf 'abc\n' | sd 'abc' 'XYZ'` → `X Y Z \n` (newline preserved). exit 0.
32	- File with **no** trailing newline: `printf 'abc noeol' > noeol.txt; sd 'abc' 'XYZ' noeol.txt`
33	  → bytes `X Y Z   n o e o l` — **no newline is added**. exit 0.
34	- Empty file (`: > empty.txt`): exit 0, stdout/stderr empty, file stays 0 bytes.
35	
36	## 3. Multiple files in one run
37	
38	```sh
39	printf 'aaa\n' > f1.txt; printf 'aaa\n' > f2.txt; printf 'aaa\n' > f3.txt
40	/workspace/executable 'aaa' 'bbb' f1.txt f2.txt f3.txt
41	```
42	- exit 0, stdout/stderr empty, all three files contain `bbb\n`. No headers,
43	  separators, or filenames are printed.
44	
45	## 4. Same file listed twice — deduplicated
46	
47	```sh
48	printf 'foo\n' > dup.txt
49	/workspace/executable 'foo' 'foofoo' dup.txt dup.txt
50	```
51	- Result: `foofoo\n` — the replacement was applied **once**, not twice
52	  (a second pass would have produced `foofoofoofoo`).
53	- With a limit: `printf 'foo foo\n' > d.txt; sd -n 1 'foo' 'X' d.txt d.txt`
54	  → `X foo\n` (exactly one replacement total).
55	- Conclusion: duplicate path arguments are deduplicated (each file processed once).
56	  exit 0, no stderr.
57	
58	## 5. No-match behavior: the file IS rewritten
59	
60	```sh
61	printf 'hello\n' > nomatch.txt
62	stat -c 'inode=%i mtime=%Y.%y' nomatch.txt   # inode=85085678 mtime=...12:41:39.81
63	sleep 1.1
64	/workspace/executable 'zzz' 'qqq' nomatch.txt; echo $?
65	```
66	- exit 0, stdout/stderr empty.
67	- After: `inode=85085691`, mtime bumped to 12:41:40.92.
68	- **Even when nothing matches, the file is replaced with an identical copy**
69	  (new inode, new mtime). Same for an invalid-UTF-8 file with no match
70	  (inode 85087294 → 85087162, mtime bumped).
71	
72	## 6. Permissions and ownership are preserved across the rewrite
73	
74	| initial mode | after `sd` | inode changed? |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| 644 | 644 | yes |
77	| 640 | 640 | yes |
78	| 600 | 600 | yes |
79	| 755 (script) | 755 | yes |
80	| 444 (read-only, in writable dir) | 444 | yes |
81	
82	- Ownership preserved: a `nobody:nogroup` file edited by root is still
83	  `nobody:nogroup` afterwards (new inode).
84	- A **read-only file (mode 444) in a writable directory is successfully replaced**
85	  (exit 0) — write permission on the file itself is not needed, because sd
86	  renames a new temp file over it.
87	
88	## 7. Write mechanism: temp file + rename in the same directory
89	
90	Evidence:
91	- Inode always changes after a successful run (even no-match).
92	- Write-failure error messages reveal the temp path (see §10), e.g.
93	  `at path "/workspace/probe/t17/locked/.tmpI6FfJI"`.
94	- Temp file naming: `.tmp` + 6 random alphanumeric chars, created in the **same
95	  directory** as the target file (e.g. `.tmpTD3IBw`, `.tmpXjmleb`, `.tmpsnlQp0`,
96	  `.tmpxIxRyS`). Cleaned up on failure (no `.tmp*` left behind).
97	- Hard links are **broken**: `ln hl1.txt hl2.txt` (links=2); after
98	  `sd 'aaa' 'bbb' hl1.txt`, `hl1.txt` has a new inode with links=1 and contains
99	  `bbb`, while `hl2.txt` keeps the old inode and old content `aaa`.
100	
101	## 8. Symlink handling
102	
103	```sh
104	printf 'target content\n' > real.txt
105	ln -s real.txt link.txt
106	/workspace/executable 'content' 'STUFF' link.txt
107	```
108	- exit 0, stderr empty. **The symlink is followed**: `real.txt` content becomes
109	  `target STUFF\n` (new inode for the target); `link.txt` remains a symlink to
110	  `real.txt` (same symlink inode). The symlink is NOT replaced by a regular file.
111	- Dangling symlink (`ln -s missing.txt dangling.txt`):
112	  - exit code: `1`, stdout empty, stderr exactly:
113	    ```
114	    error: invalid path: dangling.txt
115	    ```
116	    (bytes: `e r r o r :   i n v a l i d   p a t h :   d a n g l i n g . t x t \n`)
117	
118	## 9. Error cases: nonexistent file, directory, unreadable file
119	
120	Nonexistent file:
121	```sh
122	/workspace/executable 'a' 'b' nosuchfile.txt
123	```
124	- exit `1`, stdout empty, stderr exactly `error: invalid path: nosuchfile.txt\n`
125	
126	Directory as file arg:
127	```sh
128	mkdir somedir
129	/workspace/executable 'a' 'b' somedir
130	```
131	- exit `1`, stdout empty, stderr exactly `error: No such device (os error 19)\n`
132	  (ENODEV — consistent with attempting to mmap a directory).
133	
134	Unreadable file (`chmod 000`, run as `nobody`):
135	```sh
136	runuser -u nobody -- /workspace/executable 'secret' 'X' unread.txt
137	```
138	- exit `1`, stdout empty, stderr exactly
139	  `error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n`
140	- (As root, chmod 000 does not block root, so `runuser` was used.)
141	
142	## 10. Two error phases — validate/read aborts everything; write errors are per-file
143	
144	### Phase A: path validation + reading happens for ALL files before ANY write
145	
146	```sh
147	printf 'aaa\n' > g1.txt; printf 'aaa\n' > g3.txt
148	/workspace/executable 'aaa' 'bbb' g1.txt missing.txt g3.txt
149	```
150	- exit `1`, stderr `error: invalid path: missing.txt\n`.
151	- **Neither g1.txt nor g3.txt was modified** — even though g1.txt is listed
152	  *before* the bad file. Same result when the bad file is listed first.
153	- Two nonexistent files: only the FIRST is reported
154	  (`error: invalid path: no1.txt\n`), exit 1.
155	- A directory in the middle (`sd 'aaa' 'bbb' g1.txt d g3.txt`) behaves the same:
156	  `error: No such device (os error 19)\n`, exit 1, g1/g3 untouched.
157	- An unreadable file in the middle (as nobody): `error: Permission denied (os
158	  error 13)\n`, exit 1, the other good files untouched.
159	- Conclusion: sd first validates/reads every input; any failure in this phase
160	  aborts the whole run with a single-line `error: <message>\n` and exit 1, and
161	  **no file on the command line is modified**.
162	
163	### Phase B: write failures are aggregated; other files still processed
164	
165	Setup (all as user `nobody`): `good1.txt` and `good3.txt` in a nobody-writable
166	dir, `locked/f.txt` in a mode-555 directory.
167	```sh
168	runuser -u nobody -- /workspace/executable 'aaa' 'bbb' good1.txt locked/f.txt good3.txt
169	```
170	- exit `1`.
171	- `good1.txt` and `good3.txt` **were modified** (`bbb`); `locked/f.txt` unchanged.
172	- stderr exactly (note 4-space indent, blank line at end):
173	  ```
174	  error: Failed processing some inputs
175	      locked/f.txt: Permission denied (os error 13) at path "/workspace/probe/t17/locked/.tmpI6FfJI"
176	
177	  ```
178	- od -c of a multi-failure run shows the message ends with `"\n\n"` (a trailing
179	  blank line) and each failed input is one indented line:
180	  `    <path-as-given>: <os error> at path "<absolute temp path>"`.
181	- Failed entries are listed in argument order; processing continues past failures.
182	
183	## 11. Binary files: NUL bytes and invalid UTF-8
184	
185	NUL bytes:
186	```sh
187	printf 'foo\x00bar foo\n' > nul.bin
188	/workspace/executable 'foo' 'XXX' nul.bin
189	```
190	- exit 0, no stderr. Result bytes: `X X X \0 b a r   X X X \n` — matches across
191	  NUL are replaced, NUL preserved. File treated as binary, not skipped.
192	
193	Invalid UTF-8:
194	```sh
195	printf 'a\xff\xfe foo b\n' > badutf.bin
196	/workspace/executable 'foo' 'XXX' badutf.bin
197	```
198	- exit 0, no stderr. Result: `a 377 376   X X X   b \n` — invalid bytes passed
199	  through untouched. No error, no skipping.
200	
201	## 12. CRLF / CR files
202	
203	- `printf 'line1 foo\r\nline2 foo\r\n' > crlf.txt; sd 'foo' 'bar' crlf.txt`
204	  → `l i n e 1   b a r \r \n l i n e 2   b a r \r \n` — CRLF preserved byte-exactly.
205	- `\r\n` is matchable/replaceable: `sd '\r\n' '\n'` turns `a\r\nb\r\n` into `a\nb\n`.
206	- Lone CR preserved: `x\ry\n` with `sd 'y' 'z'` → `x\rz\n`.
207

209	
210	```sh
211	printf 'foo foo\n' > a.txt; printf 'foo foo foo\n' > b.txt
212	/workspace/executable -n 1 'foo' 'X' a.txt b.txt
213	```
214	- `a.txt` → `X foo`, `b.txt` → `X foo foo`. One replacement **per file**, not
215	  one total. exit 0.
216	
217	## 14. File arg combined with piped stdin; `-p` preview
218	
219	File arg + piped stdin:
220	```sh
221	printf 'fromfile\n' > f.txt
222	echo 'fromstdin' | /workspace/executable 'rom' 'ROM' f.txt
223	```
224	- exit 0, stdout empty, stderr empty, `f.txt` → `fROMfile`.

228	```sh
229	/workspace/executable -p 'foo' 'bar' p.txt

236	```sh

244	## 16. Very long lines / large files

246	- Single line of 2,000,003 bytes (1MB `x` + `foo` + 1MB `y`): `sd 'foo' 'BAR'`

256	
257	## Quick reference: exact error strings (all on stderr, all with trailing `\n`)
258	
259	| situation | exit | stderr |
260	|---|---|---|
261	| nonexistent file | 1 | `error: invalid path: <path>\n` |
262	| dangling symlink | 1 | `error: invalid path: <path>\n` |
263	| file named `-` missing | 1 | `error: invalid path: -\n` |
264	| directory as file | 1 | `error: No such device (os error 19)\n` |
265	| unreadable file (EACCES) | 1 | `error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n` |
266	| write failure (per file) | 1 | `error: Failed processing some inputs\n    <path>: <err> at path "<abs temp path>"\n...\n` (ends with an extra blank line) |
267	| success (any file run) | 0 | empty |
268	
269	## Summary of behavioral rules for reimplementation
270	
271	1. Parse phase: validate that every file argument exists (symlinks resolved);
272	   failure → `error: invalid path: <path>\n`, exit 1, touch nothing.
273	2. Read phase: read (mmap) every file before writing any; failure →
274	   `error: <os error>\n`, exit 1, touch nothing.
275	3. Write phase: for each file, write replaced content to `.tmpXXXXXX` (6 random
276	   alphanumerics) in the same directory, copy mode + ownership, rename over the
277	   target. Always write, even with zero replacements.
278	4. Write failures are collected; after processing all files, if any failed:
279	   print the aggregated `Failed processing some inputs` report, exit 1.
280	5. Duplicate file arguments are processed once.
281	6. File mode is silent on success; stdout is used only with `-p`.

1	# sd 1.0.0 — Preview mode (`-p` / `--preview`) behavioral spec
2	
3	Black-box probe results for `/workspace/executable` (`sd 1.0.0`). All commands run
4	on Linux (bash). Byte dumps via `od -c`. Pseudo-tty tests via `script -qec`.
5	
6	**Headline finding:** in this build, preview mode prints the *fully replaced
7	content* to stdout — byte-identical to a normal (non-preview) stdin replacement —
8	with **no ANSI colors, no diff/strikethrough display, no context chunking, no
9	gap markers, and no truncation**, under every condition tested (piped, and under
10	a real pseudo-tty with `TERM=xterm-256color` and `NO_COLOR` unset). The only
11	preview-specific formatting is a `----- FILE <path> -----` header line, printed
12	per file **only when more than one file argument is given**. Files are never
13	modified in preview mode.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. Basic stdin preview (piped)
18	
19	Command:
20	```sh
21	printf 'hello world\nfoo bar\n' | /workspace/executable -p 'world' 'WORLD' | od -c; echo $?
22	```
23	Output bytes:
24	```
25	h e l l o   W O R L D \n f o o   b a r \n
26	```
27	Exit code: `0`. stderr: empty.
28	
29	- The output is just the replaced text. No markers around the replaced region,
30	  no color, no diff of old vs new.
31	- Compare with non-preview stdin mode: byte-identical.
32	  `printf 'a foo b\n' | sd 'foo' 'X'` and `printf 'a foo b\n' | sd -p 'foo' 'X'`
33	  produce the same bytes (verified with `cmp`).
34	
35	## 2. Basic file preview
36	
37	Command:
38	```sh
39	printf 'hello world\nfoo bar\n' > t1.txt
40	/workspace/executable -p 'world' 'WORLD' t1.txt | od -c; echo $?
41	```
42	Output bytes:
43	```
44	h e l l o   W O R L D \n f o o   b a r \n
45	```
46	Exit code: `0`. **No header for a single file.** `t1.txt` afterwards still
47	contains the original `hello world\nfoo bar\n` — **preview does not modify the
48	file** (also verified via identical md5 before/after on another file).
49	
50	Single-file preview output is byte-identical to a stdin replacement of the same
51	content (`sd -p 'foo' 'X' m1.txt` == `sd 'foo' 'X' < m1.txt`, verified with `cmp`).
52	
53	## 3. Color / tty behavior
54	
55	Tested under a real pseudo-tty:
56	```sh
57	script -qec "env -u NO_COLOR TERM=xterm-256color /workspace/executable -p 'foo' 'BAR' t2.txt" /dev/null | od -c
58	```
59	(Inside the pty: `[ -t 1 ]` true, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `NO_COLOR` unset —
60	verified separately.) Also tested with `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`, and by writing the
61	script typescript to a file and dumping it (raw bytes, no pipe interference).
62	
63	Result in all cases: **zero ESC (0x1b) bytes — no ANSI color codes, ever.** The
64	only tty-induced difference is the pty's own `\n` → `\r\n` translation, which is
65	a terminal artifact, not program output.
66	
67	Also note: the deleted text is never shown either — the preview is purely the
68	post-replacement content, not an inline old+new diff.
69	
70	## 4. Multiple files: per-file headers
71	
72	Command:
73	```sh
74	printf 'a foo a\n' > m1.txt; printf 'b foo b\n' > m2.txt
75	/workspace/executable -p 'foo' 'X' m1.txt m2.txt | od -c; echo $?
76	```
77	Output bytes (exact):
78	```
79	- - - - -   F I L E   m 1 . t x t   - - - - - \n
80	a   X a \n
81	- - - - -   F I L E   m 2 . t x t   - - - - - \n
82	b   X b \n
83	```
84	Exit code: `0`. Files unchanged on disk.
85	
86	- Header format is exactly: `----- FILE ` + path-as-passed + ` -----` + `\n`
87	  (5 hyphens, space, `FILE`, space, the verbatim path string, space, 5 hyphens,
88	  newline). The path is used verbatim: `./m1.txt` prints `./m1.txt`,
89	  `/tmp/m2.txt` prints `/tmp/m2.txt` (verified).
90	- Headers appear **only when ≥2 file arguments** are given. One file → no header.
91	  Stdin → no header.
92	- No blank line or separator between one file's content and the next header —
93	  the next header follows immediately after the previous content's bytes.
94	- No trailing separator after the last file.
95	- Files with **no matches still get a header** and their content is printed
96	  unchanged:
97	  `sd -p 'foo' 'X' m1.txt m3.txt m2.txt` (m3.txt = `nothing here\n`) prints
98	  three headers, with `nothing here\n` verbatim under the second.
99	- An **empty file** in the list gets a header followed immediately by the next
100	  header (zero content bytes):
101	  `... ----- FILE empty.txt -----\n----- FILE m2.txt -----\n ...`
102	- Same headers under a pseudo-tty (modulo pty `\r\n` translation); still no ANSI.
103	
104	## 5. No matches
105	
106	```sh
107	printf 'hello world\nfoo bar\n' | /workspace/executable -p 'zzz' 'ZZZ'   # stdin
108	/workspace/executable -p 'zzz' 'ZZZ' nomatch.txt                          # file
109	```
110	Both print the input **unchanged** (`hello world\nfoo bar\n` /
111	`no match here\n`), exit code `0`, empty stderr. No "no match" message.
112	
113	## 6. Empty input
114	
115	```sh
116	printf '' | /workspace/executable -p 'x' 'Y'        # → zero output bytes, exit 0
117	printf '' > empty.txt; /workspace/executable -p 'x' 'Y' empty.txt   # → zero bytes, exit 0
118	```
119	
120	## 7. Interaction with `-n` (max replacements)
121	
122	`-n` limits are applied in preview exactly as in normal mode, per file:
123	```sh
124	printf 'foo foo foo\nfoo\n' | /workspace/executable -p -n 1 'foo' 'X'
125	# → X   f o o   f o o \n f o o \n        (exit 0)
126	printf 'foo foo foo\nfoo\n' | /workspace/executable -p -n 2 'foo' 'X'
127	# → X   X   f o o \n f o o \n
128	/workspace/executable -p -n 1 'foo' 'X' n1.txt n2.txt
129	# → ----- FILE n1.txt -----\nX   f o o\n----- FILE n2.txt -----\nX   f o o\n
130	```
131	(Per-file limit: each of n1.txt/n2.txt `foo foo\n` → `X foo\n`.) Combined short
132	flags work: `-pn 1`.
133	
134	## 8. Interaction with `-F` (fixed strings)
135	
136	```sh
137	printf 'a.b and aXb\n' | /workspace/executable -p -F 'a.b' 'Q'
138	# → Q   a n d   a X b \n        (literal match only)
139	printf 'a.b and aXb\n' | /workspace/executable -p 'a.b' 'Q'
140	# → Q   a n d   Q \n            (regex: both matched)
141	```
142	-F with a literal newline in the pattern also matches across lines:
143	```sh
144	printf 'start\nmid\nend\n' | /workspace/executable -p -F "$(printf 'start\nmid')" 'JOINED'
145	# → J O I N E D \n e n d \n   (exit 0)
146	```

149	
150	Multi-line matching is on by default; preview shows the joined result with no

158	
159	```sh

161	# → X a X b X \n X        (exit 0)
162	printf 'ab\n' | /workspace/executable -p 'x*' '-'

167	## 11. Large input — no chunking, no truncation, no context lines
168	
169	- 220-line file with matches every 25 lines
170	  (`line N MATCH here` / `line N plain`):
171	  `sd -p 'MATCH' 'HIT' big220.txt` → output is **exactly 220 lines**, the full
172	  replaced file. **No `-----` separators, no context filtering, no gap/merge
173	  markers** (`grep -c -- '-----'` = 0). Same via stdin: 220 lines out.
174	- 200,000-line / ~3.5 MB file, match every 1000 lines:
175	  output size = input size adjusted only for the 200 replacements; `cmp` against
176	  `sed 's/MATCH/HIT/g'` of the input → identical. **No truncation.**
177	
178	## 12. Byte fidelity / encoding
179	
180	- Missing trailing newline is preserved (no newline added):
181	  `printf 'foo no newline' | sd -p 'foo' 'X'` → `X   n o   n e w l i n e`
182	  (12 bytes, no `\n`), same for a file.
183	- CRLF preserved verbatim: file `a\r\nb foo\r\n` → `a\r\nb X\r\n`.
184	- Non-UTF-8 bytes pass through untouched: file `a\xffb foo\n` → `a\xffb X\n`,
185	  exit 0.
186	
187	## 13. Read-only files, stdin/file precedence
188	
189	- Preview of a read-only file (`chmod 444`) succeeds (no write attempted):
190	  prints replaced content, exit 0.
191	- When file arguments are given, stdin is ignored:
192	  `echo stdin-ignored | sd -p 'foo' 'X' m1.txt` → prints only m1.txt's preview.
193	
194	## 14. Errors and exit codes
195	
196	- Nonexistent file: `/workspace/executable -p 'foo' 'X' m1.txt /does/not/exist.txt`
197	  → **no stdout at all** (validated upfront, before any preview output);
198	  stderr: `error: invalid path: /does/not/exist.txt\n`; exit code `1`.
199	- Directory as file arg: stderr `error: No such device (os error 19)\n`; exit `1`.
200	- Invalid regex: `printf 'x' | sd -p '(' 'X'` → stderr:
201	  ```
202	  error: invalid regex regex parse error:
203	      (
204	      ^
205	  error: unclosed group
206	  ```
207	  exit `1`.
208	- All successful preview runs (match, no-match, empty, multi-file, huge):
209	  exit `0`, stderr empty.
210	
211	## 15. Reimplementation checklist (exact)
212	
213	1. `-p`/`--preview`: write replaced content to **stdout**, never touch the files.
214	2. If reading from stdin OR exactly one file: print only the replaced content,
215	   byte-exact (preserve missing trailing newline, CRLF, non-UTF-8 bytes).
216	3. If ≥2 files: before each file's content print
217	   `----- FILE <verbatim-path> -----\n`. Print for every file including
218	   no-match and empty ones. Nothing between files, nothing after the last.
219	4. Never emit ANSI escape codes (regardless of tty/TERM/NO_COLOR).
220	5. No chunking/context/gap logic — always the full replaced content.
221	6. `-n` limit applies per file; `-F` works as in normal mode.
222	7. No matches → content printed unchanged, exit 0, silent.
223	8. Empty input → empty output, exit 0.
224	9. Bad path / unreadable file → `error: ...` on stderr, exit 1, no partial stdout.
225	10. Exit 0 on success; stderr empty on success.

1	# sd 1.0.0 — stdio behavioral probe report
2	
3	Binary: `/workspace/executable` (`sd 1.0.0`). All probes were black-box: command-line, stdin/stdout/stderr, and files only.
4	All byte dumps are from `od -c`. Exit codes captured via `echo $?` / `PIPESTATUS`.
5	Note: the probing shell had `NO_COLOR=1` and `TERM=dumb` pre-set; tests that matter were repeated with those unset/overridden.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. stdin source variants
10	
11	### 1a. stdin closed (`</dev/null`)
12	```
13	$ /workspace/executable a b </dev/null
14	exit=0, stdout: (empty, 0 bytes), stderr: (empty)
15	```
16	
17	### 1b. empty pipe
18	```
19	$ printf '' | /workspace/executable a b
20	exit=0, stdout: (empty), stderr: (empty)
21	```
22	
23	### 1c. piped data
24	```
25	$ printf 'hello a world\n' | /workspace/executable a b
26	exit=0, stdout: h e l l o   b   w o r l d \n
27	```
28	
29	### 1d. redirected file (`sd a b < file`)
30	```
31	$ printf 'foo a bar\n' > in4.txt; /workspace/executable a b < in4.txt
32	exit=0, stdout: f o o   b   b a r \n
33	```
34	Identical transformation to in-place file mode (`sd a b file` produces the same bytes in the file).
35	
36	### 1e. stdin is a TTY
37	sd does **not** detect or special-case a tty; it reads stdin until EOF like any other source.
38	- Under `script -qec '/workspace/executable a b' /dev/null` with stdin from `/dev/null`: immediate EOF, exit=0, no output.
39	- With delayed input fed through the pty:
40	  ```
41	  $ (sleep 1; printf 'x a y\n'; sleep 0.5) | timeout 5 script -qec '/workspace/executable a b' /dev/null
42	  exit=0, captured pty output: x   a   y \r\n  x   b   y \r\n
43	  ```
44	  (first `x a y\r\n` is the pty's own echo; `x b y\r\n` is sd's output with the pty's `\n`→`\r\n` translation).
45	- With no input ever sent, sd blocks reading the tty (confirmed via 3 s wait; it only exited when the pty closed). **It would block forever on an interactive tty until Ctrl-D.**
46

49	## 2. Trailing-newline handling on stdout
50	
51	Output byte count exactly tracks the input — **no newline is ever added or removed**.
52	
53	```
54	$ printf 'no newline a' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
55	n o   n e w l i n e   b            (12 bytes, NO trailing \n), exit=0
56	$ printf 'with newline a\n' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
57	w i t h   n e w l i n e   b \n     (trailing \n preserved)
58	$ printf 'a' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
59	b                                    (1 byte)
60	```
61	
62	## 3. CRLF passthrough
63	
64	```
65	$ printf 'line1 a\r\nline2\r\n' | /workspace/executable a b | od -c
66	l i n e 1   b \r\n l i n e 2 \r\n
67	```
68	CRLF preserved byte-for-byte. Note: `$` anchors are **not** CRLF-aware:
69	```
70	$ printf 'a\r\nb\r\n' | /workspace/executable 'a$' 'X' | od -c
71	a \r\n b \r\n        (unchanged — 'a$' does not match before \r\n)
72	```
73	
74	## 4. NUL bytes and invalid UTF-8
75	
76	Both are passed through untouched, exit=0, no error, no replacement char. Matching still works around them (the regex engine is byte-oriented but Unicode-aware).
77	
78	```
79	$ printf 'a\0b a c\n' | /workspace/executable a Z | od -c
80	Z \0 b   Z   c \n                          exit=0, stderr empty
81	$ printf 'x\0y\n' | /workspace/executable -F 'x' 'Q' | od -c
82	Q \0 y \n
83	$ printf 'good \xff\xfe a end\n' | /workspace/executable a Z | od -c
84	g o o d   377 376   Z   e n d \n           exit=0, stderr empty (same with -F)
85	$ printf 'p\x80q\n' | /workspace/executable p q | od -c
86	q 200 q \n
87	```
88	
89	Regex `.` over these bytes:
90	```
91	$ printf 'x\xffy\n' | /workspace/executable 'x.y' 'M' | od -c
92	x 377 y \n        (NO match — '.' does not match an invalid-UTF-8 byte)
93	$ printf 'x\0y\n' | /workspace/executable 'x.y' 'M' | od -c
94	M \n              (match — '.' DOES match NUL, a valid codepoint U+0000)
95	```
96	(Consistent with a `regex::bytes`-style engine with Unicode mode on.)
97	
98	## 5. Zero matches
99	
100	Output = input, byte-identical (including absence of trailing newline). Exit 0. stdout is still written.
101	
102	```
103	$ printf 'nothing here\n' | /workspace/executable zzz qqq | od -c
104	n o t h i n g   h e r e \n        exit=0
105	$ printf 'nothing here' | /workspace/executable zzz qqq | od -c
106	n o t h i n g   h e r e           (no trailing newline added)
107	$ printf '' | /workspace/executable zzz qqq | od -c
108	(empty)                             exit=0
109	```
110	
111	Zero-match **file** in-place: the file is still rewritten (mtime updated to now) even though content is unchanged:
112	```
113	$ touch -d '2020-01-01' z.txt; /workspace/executable zzz qqq z.txt
114	exit=0; mtime after: 2026-08-10 ...; content byte-identical
115	```
116	
117	## 6. Buffering / streaming model
118	
119	**sd reads ALL of stdin before writing ANY output.** It is not streaming.
120	
121	- Delayed-input test: `(printf 'first a\n'; sleep 2; printf 'second a\n') | sd a b | timestamp-each-line` — both output lines arrived at the same timestamp (~2 s in), i.e. after stdin EOF.
122	- 50 MB pipe: `cat big50.bin | sd a b > out` — 52,428,800 bytes in, 52,428,800 out, byte-identical to expected (every `a` replaced), exit 0, ~1.05 s wall.
123	- Peak RSS (polled `/proc/$pid/status` VmHWM) for the 50 MB run: **107,752 kB ≈ 105 MB** — about 2× the input size (full input buffer + full output buffer in memory).
124	- Consequence: infinite stdin (e.g. `yes`) never terminates — see §7.
125	
126	## 7. Broken pipe on stdout
127	
128	```
129	$ set -o pipefail; cat big50.bin | /workspace/executable a b | head -c 5
130	head got: b b c   b        (first 5 bytes)
131	PIPESTATUS = 0 1 0         (sd exit code = 1)
132	sd stderr (exact bytes): e r r o r :   B r o k e n   p i p e   ( o s   e r r o r   3 2 ) \n
133	```
134	i.e. the literal 33-byte line:
135	```
136	error: Broken pipe (os error 32)
137	```
138	Exit code on EPIPE = **1** (no panic, no 101). SIGPIPE is evidently ignored/handled (Rust default).
139	
140	With an **infinite** producer the consumer closing does not help, because sd never finishes reading stdin:
141	```
142	$ timeout 3 bash -c 'yes "match a" | /workspace/executable a b 2>/dev/null | head -c 5'
143	exit=124          (timed out — sd hangs reading stdin forever)
144	```
145	
146	Other write-side errors use the same format:
147	```
148	$ printf 'a\n' | /workspace/executable a b > /dev/full
149	exit=1, stderr: error: No space left on device (os error 28)\n
150	```
151	
152	## 8. Files AND stdin both given — precedence
153	
154	**File arguments win; stdin is ignored completely** (never read, never a fallback):
155	
156	```
157	$ printf 'file content a\n' > f1.txt
158	$ printf 'stdin content a\n' | /workspace/executable a b f1.txt
159	exit=0, stdout: (empty), stderr: (empty)
160	f1.txt afterwards: f i l e   c o n t e n t   b \n     (modified in place; stdin untouched)
161	```
162	Even with a nonexistent file there is no stdin fallback:
163	```
164	$ printf 'stdin a\n' | /workspace/executable a b /no/such
165	exit=1, stdout: (empty), stderr: error: invalid path: /no/such\n
166	```
167	A `-` argument is treated as a literal filename, not stdin:
168	```
169	$ printf 'a\n' | /workspace/executable a b -
170	exit=1, stderr: error: invalid path: -\n
171	```

173	## 9. Error-message encoding on stderr
174	
175	All error messages are plain ASCII, no ANSI color/attributes — **even when stderr is a tty** (verified under `script`; only the pty's `\n`→`\r\n` translation appeared). Exact strings:
176	
177	- Invalid regex (exit 1):
178	  ```
179	  error: invalid regex parse error:
180	      (
181	      ^
182	  error: unclosed group
183	  ```
184	  Exact bytes: `error: invalid regex parse error:\n    (\n    ^\nerror: unclosed group\n`
185	- Nonexistent path (exit 1): `error: invalid path: /nonexistent/path.txt\n`
186	- Directory as file arg (exit 1): `error: No such device (os error 19)\n`
187	- Broken pipe (exit 1): `error: Broken pipe (os error 32)\n`
188	- /dev/full (exit 1): `error: No space left on device (os error 28)\n`
189	- Missing required CLI arg (exit **2**, clap usage error):
190	  ```
191	  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
192	    <REPLACE_WITH>
193	
194	  Usage: executable <FIND> <REPLACE_WITH> [FILES]...
195	
196	  For more information, try '--help'.
197	  ```
198	
199	Exit-code summary: 0 = success (including zero matches, empty input); 1 = runtime errors (regex compile, I/O, invalid path, broken pipe); 2 = CLI usage errors; 101 = panic (documented in man page; not triggered by any probe here — e.g. an out-of-range capture ref `'(a)' → '$2'` did NOT panic, it replaced with the empty string: `printf 'a\n' | sd '(a)' '$2'` → `\n`, exit 0).

201	## 10. Environment variables / preview colors
202	
203	Preview mode (`-p`) writes the full would-be-new content to stdout and leaves the file untouched. **No ANSI color codes are emitted in any configuration tested**, and no env var had any observable effect on output bytes:
204	
205	| Configuration | Output bytes |
206	|---|---|
207	| `-p`, stdout=pipe | plain text, no escapes |
208	| `-p`, stdout=tty (`script`) | plain text, no escapes |
209	| `-p`, tty, `NO_COLOR` unset, `TERM=xterm-256color` | identical plain text |
210	| `-p`, tty, `TERM=dumb` | identical plain text |
211	| `-p`, pipe, `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` | identical plain text |
212	| `-p`, pipe, `NO_COLOR=1` (default env) | identical plain text |
213	
214	```
215	$ script -qec 'env -u NO_COLOR TERM=xterm-256color /workspace/executable -p a b pv.txt' /dev/null | od -c
216	b l p h b   b   o m e g b \r\n s e c o n d   l i n e   b \r\n     (no ESC bytes anywhere)
217	```
218	So for reimplementation: preview output = transformed content, colors never appear; `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `COLORTERM` are all inert. (`-p` with stdin behaves the same as normal stdin→stdout mode.)
219	
220	## 11. Misc stdio-adjacent findings
221	
222	- Empty pattern: `printf 'ab\n' | sd '' 'X'` → `X a X b X \n X` (6 bytes `XaXbX\nX`) — empty regex matches at every position including after the final `\n`; exit 0.
223	- `--` end-of-flags works with stdin: `printf 'foo -w\n' | sd -- '-w' 'X'` → `foo X\n`.
224	- sd replaces **all** occurrences (default `-n 0` = unlimited), including inside words: `abc a def` → `bbc b def` with `sd a b`.
225	- stdout writes happen only after full stdin EOF, then the complete transformed buffer is written (single-pass, not chunked per line).

228	
229	## 10-line summary — most important/surprising findings
230	
231	1. sd reads ALL of stdin into memory before writing a single byte — with `yes` it hangs forever even after the consumer closes the pipe (timeout 124).
232	2. Memory footprint ≈ 2× input size (50 MB input → ~105 MB peak RSS); output written in one shot after EOF.
233	3. Broken pipe: exit code 1 with exact stderr line `error: Broken pipe (os error 32)\n` — no panic, no SIGPIPE death.
234	4. Byte-exact passthrough: never adds/removes a trailing newline; CRLF preserved verbatim; NUL and invalid UTF-8 (`\xff`, `\x80`) pass through untouched with exit 0.
235	5. Regex `.` matches NUL but NOT invalid-UTF-8 bytes (byte-oriented, Unicode-aware engine).
236	6. Zero matches still write full output (stdin mode) and still rewrite the file (mtime bumps) in file mode — exit 0 either way.
237	7. File args completely override stdin: piped stdin is silently ignored when files are given, even if the file doesn't exist; `-` is a literal filename, not stdin.
238	8. TTY stdin is not detected at all — sd blocks reading until EOF (Ctrl-D), same as a pipe.
239	9. Error messages are plain ASCII with no ANSI color even on a tty; exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime/IO/regex errors, 2 clap usage errors; `$2`-style out-of-range group refs yield empty string, not a panic.
240	10. `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` have zero observable effect — preview mode (`-p`) never emits ANSI colors; it just prints the transformed content to stdout without modifying the file.
